                snap.downloads.get(id).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
            )
        };

            return div().into_any_element();

            if m.active { "downloaded ✓ active ✓" } else { "downloaded ✓" }
        } else if m.present {
            "partial"
        } else {
            "missing"
        };
        let store_d = store.clone();
        let store_c = store.clone();

**Tool Call: present-voice\app\src\theme.rs**
Status: Completed

//! Present Voice palette + theme application.
//!
//! Neutrals are true grays (no blue tint — the old tinted navbar is
//! gone); per-mode helpers serve our custom chrome while kit widgets follow
//! `Theme::change`. Functional blues get a slight desaturation pass so the
//! whole UI reads calmer.

use gpui_kit::component::theme::{Theme, ThemeMode};
use gpui_kit::{App, Hsla};

/// Keep 85% of blue saturation on functional accents.
pub const BLUE_DESAT: f32 = 0.85;

pub const BG_DARK: u32 = 0x17_17_17_ff;
pub const SURFACE_DARK: u32 = 0x21_21_21_ff;
pub const FG_DARK: u32 = 0xe8_e8_e8_ff;
/// Light surfaces (true neutral).
pub const BG_LIGHT: u32 = 0xf5_f5_f5_ff;
pub const SURFACE_LIGHT: u32 = 0xff_ff_ff_ff;
pub const FG_LIGHT: u32 = 0x17_17_17_ff;

pub fn bg(dark: bool) -> u32 {
    if dark {
        BG_DARK
    } else {
        BG_LIGHT
    }
}

pub fn fg(dark: bool) -> u32 {
    if dark {
        FG_DARK
    } else {
        FG_LIGHT
    }
}

pub fn surface(dark: bool) -> u32 {
    if dark {
        SURFACE_DARK
    } else {
        SURFACE_LIGHT
    }
}

/// Pure color math: scale saturation, keep hue/lightness/alpha.
pub fn desat(c: Hsla, keep: f32) -> Hsla {
    Hsla {
        s: (c.s * keep).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
        ..c
    }
}

/// Apply the mode to kit widgets, then calm the functional blues.
/// Call on boot (after `init`) and on every toggle.
pub fn apply_theme(dark: bool, cx: &mut App) {
    Theme::change(
        if dark {
            ThemeMode::Dark
        } else {
            ThemeMode::Light
        },
        None,
        cx,
    );
    let colors = &mut Theme::global_mut(cx).colors;
    for slot in [
        &mut colors.selection,
        &mut colors.link,
        &mut colors.link_active,
        &mut colors.link_hover,
        &mut colors.drag_border,
        &mut colors.drop_target,
    ] {
        *slot = desat(*slot, BLUE_DESAT);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn desat_keeps_hue_lightness_alpha() {
        let c = Hsla {
            h: 0.6,
            s: 0.8,
            l: 0.5,
            a: 1.0,
        };
        let d = desat(c, 0.85);
        assert_eq!((d.h, d.l, d.a), (0.6, 0.5, 1.0));
        assert!((d.s - 0.68).abs() < 1e-6);
    }

    #[test]
    fn desat_clamps() {
        let c = Hsla {
            h: 0.0,
            s: 2.0,
            l: 0.5,
            a: 1.0,
        };
        assert_eq!(desat(c, 2.0).s, 1.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mode_helpers_split() {
        assert_ne!(bg(true), bg(false));
        assert_ne!(fg(true), fg(false));
        assert_ne!(surface(true), surface(false));
    }
}

# Audacity

[](#audacity)

[![Coverage](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/c5a893cc12fc13e450e033e6eee690b2e902f3962c54b58c86f3627555fadb62/68747470733a2f2f73332e75732d656173742d312e616d617a6f6e6177732e636f6d2f657874656e73696f6e732e6d75736573636f72652e6f72672f746573742f636f64655f636f7665726167652f61755f636f7665726167655f62616467652e737667)](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/actions/workflows/au4_check_unit_tests.yml)

[**Audacity**](https://www.audacityteam.org) is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. More info can be found on [https://www.audacityteam.org](https://www.audacityteam.org)

## This repository is currently undergoing major structural change.

[](#this-repository-is-currently-undergoing-major-structural-change)

We're currently working on Audacity 4, which means an entirely new UI and also refactorings aplenty. As such, the `master` branch is currently not particularly friendly to new contributors. It is still possible to submit patches to Audacity 3.x; make sure you branch off `audacity3` if you choose to do so. Build instructions for 3.x can be found [here](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/blob/release-3.7.0/BUILDING.md); build instructions for Audacity 4 can be found [here](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/blob/master/BUILDING.md).

You can stay updated with our efforts on [YouTube](https://youtube.com/@audacity), [Discord](https://discord.gg/audacity) and [our blog](https://audacityteam.org/blog).

## License

[](#license)

Audacity is open source software licensed GPLv3. Most code files are GPLv2-or-later, with the notable exceptions being `/au3/lib-src` (which contains third party libraries), as well as VST3-related code. Documentation is licensed CC-by 3.0 unless otherwise noted. Details can be found in the [license file](/audacity/audacity/blob/master/LICENSE.txt).

## Assistant

## Plan — In-app voice recording (Audacity-style) + page scroll + collapsible window

Read-only; no files touched (plan mode).

### 1. What Audacity actually does (and what we borrow)

Audacity (`github.com/audacity/audacity`, GPL — **do not copy code**, borrow the architecture only):

- Capture via **PortAudio** → host API (**WASAPI** on Windows / CoreAudio / ALSA). Opens the default input device, captures **32-bit float** at device rate, routes through a mixer with input-level monitoring + overdub, writes to its project DB (`aup3`/SQLite) with crash-recovery journaling.
- What we need is ~5% of that: **mono voice capture → plain `.wav` on disk → existing transcribe pipeline**. No multitrack, no effects, no `aup3`. Our equivalent of PortAudio in Rust is **`cpal`** (WASAPI/CoreAudio/ALSA backends, no GPL, matches our offline native story). WAV writing via **`hound`** (pure Rust, 16-bit PCM), output **16 kHz mono `.wav` by default** so it drops straight into `load_audio_16k`'s fast path (`audio_ffmpeg.cpp:353` — no ffmpeg conversion needed).

### 2. Record page (separate from Transcribe)

New `Page::Record` + `views_record.rs`, nav order **Input · Record · Output · Models · Settings** so recording is never confused with batch transcription:

- **Layout (theme-matched):** same `theme::bg/surface/fg` + `FontWeight::SEMIBOLD` buttons as Input; top row device picker (dropdown of `cpal` input devices + default) + sample-rate label; big **● Record / ■ Stop / ⏸ Pause-Resume** row; live level meter (RMS bar via existing `Progress` widget pattern) + elapsed timer + peak-clip indicator; footer status line reuses `Store.status` style.
- **Flow:** Record → `<data>/recordings/Rec <date> <time>.wav` (streaming write, header finalized on Stop) → on Stop show **"Send to Input for transcription"** (queues into existing `Store.input` / `queue_files`) + **"Reveal in folder"** + **"Discard"**. Recording never auto-transcribes — user explicitly sends it, keeping Record vs Transcribe separate per your spec.
- **Format:** default **WAV 16 kHz mono 16-bit** written directly at capture (resample in the callback when the device runs at 44.1/48 kHz — simple linear/box resample is fine for voice; exact offline resample can ride the existing ffmpeg path if needed). This satisfies "raw wav by default instead of aup3" and means zero conversion before STT.
- **Safety:** exclusive-access errors (device busy), denied mic permission, and device-unplug mid-take each surface in the Error Center with the Audacity-equivalent remedy ("close the app using the mic / check Settings → Privacy → Microphone"); partial take is kept as `.wav` + never auto-deleted. Recording auto-stops (file kept) on app quit via the existing quit-hook path — add `recorder.stop()` before `abort_all`.
- **Deps:** `cpal = "0.15"` + `hound = "3"` in a new `pv-backend/src/record.rs` (device enum, level callback, atomic stop flag) — no new system DLLs, no network, Windows privacy prompt handled by OS. Crash-recovery journal (Audacity's `aup3`-journal) is overkill; streaming WAV + finalized header on Stop is enough since a killed take is still a playable WAV up to the last flushed block.

### 3. Scrollbars fitted to window (Input / Output / Models)

Today only Output's tree scrolls — and with a **fixed `h(px(560.))`** (`views_output.rs:396-403`), which breaks fit on small windows. Input/Models have bare `flex_1` chains with no scroll container, so content overflows with no wheel target; root (`views.rs:131-154`) has no viewport bound (same root cause as the Settings issue).

Fix pattern (same 3-line recipe per page, inside the existing bounded-body wrapper from the Settings plan):

- Root gets the viewport bound (`size_full` + body wrapped in `flex_1.min_h_0.overflow_hidden`); each page's long region becomes `div().flex_1().min_h_0().overflow_y_scrollbar().id("<page>-scroll")` — replace Output's fixed `h(560)` with `flex_1/min_h_0` so it shrinks/grows with the window; add equivalent containers to Input (staged-file list + progress block) and Models (tier panel + Speech|Text columns + Ollama list). Nav stays `flex_shrink_0`.
- `ScrollableElement` import already exists on Output/Settings; add to Input/Models/Record. `smoke.mjs` gains asserts for `record-scroll/input-scroll/out-tree/models-scroll` + "no fixed pixel heights in page scroll containers."

### 4. Shrink-to-title-bar (feature, not bug)

Explicitly allow it: set **`WindowOptions.window_min_size` to ~tile (`px(240.), px(64.)`)** instead of a 900×600 floor, make the nav row `flex_wrap` + `flex_shrink_0`, and ensure every scroll container has `min_h_0` so collapsing to just nav+titlebar never panics on zero/negative height (GPUI lays out empty scroll regions fine; guard the level-meter + progress math against divide-by-zero at tiny widths). At title-bar size the user sees nav only; expanding restores scroll positions (ids are stable). Document in Settings → About line: "Window collapses to title bar by design."

### Build order + verification

1. `pv-backend/record.rs` (cpal+hound, unit-tested WAV header/size) → 2. `Page::Record` + nav + theme → 3. Stop→Send-to-Input handoff + quit-hook auto-stop → 4. Scroll-container retrofit (Input/Output/Models/Record) + min-size change → 5. `cargo check/test --workspace` + `node tests/smoke.mjs` + manual: record 10 s → WAV plays → Send to Input → transcribe; shrink window to title bar and back on each page with no panic.

### Questions

1. WAV default confirmed as **16 kHz mono 16-bit** (fastest STT path)? Or 48 kHz archival with auto-convert on transcribe?
2. Record page extras in v1: input-device picker + level meter enough, or also mic-privacy status line and take-renaming before send?
3. Hotkey for Record/Stop (e.g. `Ctrl-R`) alongside existing `Ctrl-Space` pause — wanted?


## User

make sure the audio files (through a setting) either get deleted on completion of the summary, or put into the same output file as the transcript summary. wav files should be 24 bit with a pass to compress the file before transcription to get rid of empty noise. record page should mirror audacity's modern one in night theme and old theme in white one if you are familliar, if not do a simple reactionary waveform like https://github.com/jeffvli/feishin with general buttons "play", "pause", "stop", "record", "clear", "send to queue", if user does not press send to queue have it automatically get sent to the input page when they move to the input page. make sure that recording length is recorded, and the recording status, no hotkeys, buttonpress only (unless they are on the same page which can be an exception but don't bother it since it complicates things). thoughts and questions

<thinking>
Designing a three-state audio retention setting and clarifying 24-bit WAV handling with STT preprocessing.

## Thoughts + plan (read-only, no changes made)

### 1. Audio retention setting — delete vs. bundle

Today `delete_converted` (`store.rs:1431-1442`, `prefs.rs:85-87`, `pipeline.cpp:518-523`) only deletes the **converted cache copy**, never the user's original. Your spec needs a true 3-state setting, e.g. `Settings → Recordings & sources`:

- `Keep originals` (current default — nothing deleted)
- `Delete sources on success` (delete the **source file listed on the job** after `PV_DONE`; failed/aborted/retried files never touched — same guard as today's cache rule)
- `Archive beside output` (copy the source `.wav` to `<output>/<stem>.src.wav` next to the `.md` + sidecars, then optionally delete the original — bury the choice as a sub-checkbox "delete original after archiving")

One clarification baked into the plan: a `.wav` can't literally live *inside* a Markdown file — the "same output file" is implemented as **same stem, same folder** (`Title.md` + `Title.src.wav` + `Title.md.json`), and the `.md` gets an `## Audio` line linking the filename. Originals outside the job (e.g. user-recorded takes still on the Record page) are never deleted by the transcription path — only the queued source copy is eligible, and only on success.

### 2. 24-bit WAV + denoise pass before STT

Agreed, with one split:

- **Archival capture = 24-bit** as you said (`hound` 24-bit PCM, device rate or 48 kHz mono). Reader already supports 24-bit (`audio_ffmpeg.cpp:205-210` PCM24 branch) so nothing breaks.
- **STT feed stays 16 kHz mono float** (`internal.h:24`, fast path `load_audio_16k:353`). So the "pass to compress before transcription" becomes a pure-C++ DSP stage in `core/` between load and `stt_transcribe`: DC-offset remove → **noise gate** (silence/room-tone suppression with attack/release so speech onsets aren't clipped) → peak-normalize → light **compressor** (2:1 above −12 dBFS, no makeup beyond unity — voice intelligibility, not mastering loudness) → downmix to 16 k mono. Deterministic, no new DLLs, gate threshold + on/off in Settings with "keep archival 24-bit untouched; only the STT copy is processed" documented. Edge cases: all-silence take → warn instead of transcribing air; clipped takes → clip counter in status; gate settings logged per-file for repro. Unit tests on synthetic WAVs (silence trim length, 24-bit round-trip, gate doesn't eat soft consonants).

### 3. Record page look + behavior

- **Theme mapping:** reuse `theme.rs` tokens — night (Audacity-modern-dark equivalent): `BG_DARK 0x171717 / SURFACE 0x212121 / FG 0xe8e8e8`, desaturated blue accents; light: `BG 0xf5f5f5 / SURFACE white / FG 0x171717` (Audacity-classic-light equivalent). No new palette — Record reads `dark_mode` like every page.
- **Waveform:** Feishin-style reactive view — a lightweight custom canvas element fed by the recorder's peak ring-buffer (per-~50 ms RMS/peak, downsampled columns), dark: gray-blue bars on near-black with red clip ticks; light: gray bars on white. Playback cursor sweeps on Play; while recording the trace appends live. Zero-height guard so title-bar collapse can't divide by zero.
- **Transport row exactly:** `Record ● / Play ▶ / Pause ❚❚ / Stop ■ / Clear / Send to queue` — `Button` widgets, `SEMIBOLD`, danger-accent on Record. State machine: `Empty → Recording ⇄ Paused → Stopped(unsent take) → Sent`. Play works on the stopped take (and on any selected take); Clear discards only after confirm and only when not recording; `Send to queue` moves the WAV path into `Store.input` (existing `queue_files` path) and marks the take sent.
- **Auto-send on nav:** hook page-change (`RootView::goto` + `store.page` setter): if leaving Record with an unsent finished take, auto-stage it to Input and toast "Take sent to Input." Never auto-send mid-recording — navigating away while recording keeps capturing (status dot stays in nav) or prompts Stop; quit auto-stops and keeps the file (existing quit-hook ordering: `recorder.stop()` → drafts/prefs flush → `abort_all` → exit).
- **Length + status (always visible):** header line `● REC 00:03:12 · 24-bit/48 kHz mono · peak −6 dB` / `❚❚ PAUSED 00:01:02` / `▶ PLAYING 00:00:44/00:03:12` / `■ STOPPED — unsent take 00:03:12` / `Empty — press Record`. Timer ticks from the audio callback sample count (not wall clock, so pause is exact).
- **No hotkeys:** confirmed — no `KeyBinding` for transport; buttons only. (Agreed, skip the same-page exception; keeps focus/keymap conflicts at zero.)

### Build order

1. `pv-backend/record.rs` (cpal capture + hound 24-bit + peaks) → 2. DSP gate/compress stage in `core/` → 3. retention 3-state pref + archive/delete plumbing → 4. `views_record.rs` + nav + auto-send hook → 5. scroll-container retrofit shared with the earlier window-fit work → `cargo test` + `smoke.mjs` + manual record→play→send→transcribe pass.

3. Record sample rate: fixed 48 kHz mono 24-bit, or follow the input device's native rate?

## Locked in + thoughts (still read-only, no changes)

### 1. Archive beside `.md` — confirmed

`<Title>.md` + `<Title>.src.wav` + `<Title>.md.json` in the same output folder, with an `## Audio` line in the `.md` naming the wav. No subfolder, no embedding. Delete-original-after-archive stays a sub-checkbox, default off; only successful outputs are eligible.

### 2. Denoise: adaptive in-app — and yes, Realtek/Windows already do some of this, which is exactly why ours stays ours

You're right that many Windows machines already have a denoise layer:

- **Realtek Audio Console** (OEM-dependent) ships "noise suppression" / "AI noise cancellation" on recent drivers — but only on machines with that driver + console installed, settings vary per OEM, and it applies at the capture endpoint opaquely (we can't query or control it).
- **Windows itself** has mic noise suppression paths (classic enhancements tab + Win11 voice-clarity on supported hardware) — again per-device, per-driver, user-toggleable outside our app.

So the plan treats those as **unreliable environment**, not a dependency:

- Our pass stays **adaptive**: measure the first ~0.5–1 s (or quietest decile) as the noise floor per take, set gate threshold relative to it (e.g. floor + 6–9 dB with attack/release + hangover so soft consonants survive), then light 2:1 compression above −12 dBFS. Per-file floor/threshold logged for repro.
- Settings gets a 3-way `Denoise: Recommended (adaptive) / Off / Aggressive` — **Recommended = default**, matching your call. Off exists for studio-quiet mics and for users who already run Realtek suppression and hear double-gating artifacts (we'll note that in the helper text: *"If your voice sounds clipped and Realtek/Windows mic effects are on, try Off"*).
- Archival 24-bit take is never processed — only the 16 kHz mono STT copy goes through the gate. Skip-summary/raw path keeps raw untouched.

### 3. Sample rate follows the device + picker can request changes — agreed

- Capture opens the selected input at **its native/default rate** (no forced resample at record time); rate + channels + bit depth shown live in the status line (`48 kHz · mono · 24-bit` etc.).
- Device picker lists `cpal` inputs with their supported configs; selecting a device shows its available rates and lets the user pick one **the device reports as supported** — we call `try_with_sample_rate`, and if the driver refuses we fall back to device default and toast why. Never request an unsupported rate (that's what causes exclusive-mode `InvalidArgument` errors).
- Resample to 16 kHz mono happens only in the pre-STT pass, not at capture — archival stays native.

### Remaining questions (small, then the plan is build-ready)

1. **Adaptive floor source:** measure from a short leading-silence window at take start (simplest, needs ~1 s of room tone — we can prompt "a moment of silence…"), or continuous tracking throughout the take (handles AC kicking on mid-lecture, slightly more code)? I recommend continuous with a slow follower; confirm?
2. **Aggressive preset bounds:** cap it at the same 2:1 compressor with a higher gate (+12 dB over floor), or allow heavier NR that risks voice thinning? I recommend capped — confirm?
3. **Metering:** peak-hold + clip counter enough, or also show the live noise-floor estimate (nice for "is my room too loud" feedback)?

If those three land, the full build sequence from the last two messages is ready to execute on your go-ahead.

## Assistant

## Agreed — background-adaptive, all "recommended" — final shape

**Adaptive design, locked:**

- **First ~60 s = calibration window.** Gate runs in background learning mode from take start: tracks the quietest-decile energy as the noise floor, holds the gate conservative (low threshold, long hangover) so no speech is eaten while it learns. Status line shows a subtle `learning room tone…` hint during this window.
- **After minute one = slow follower + drastic-change re-adapt.** Slow follower (seconds-scale smoothing) rides gradual drift (AC hum, room warming up). A **drastic-change detector** (floor jumps >~10 dB sustained ~2–3 s, e.g. door slams, HVAC kicks on, mic moved) triggers a bounded re-learn (~3–5 s, gate temporarily conservative again) and logs `noise floor re-adapted at MM:SS (old→new dB)` per file for the audit trail. No full 60 s re-calibration — just the short window, so speech loss is bounded.
- **Presets = Recommended everywhere:** Denoise `Recommended (adaptive)` default; Aggressive capped (higher gate, same gentle 2:1 compressor — no voice-thinning NR); metering = peak-hold + clip counter + live floor readout (your third "recommended" — the floor readout doubles as "is my room too loud" feedback and makes the re-adapt events legible).

**Why this is the right call:** leading-silence-only calibration breaks the moment the room changes mid-lecture; continuous fast adaptation eats soft consonants. Background-learn-then-guard is the middle path — conservative when uncertain, quick only when the evidence (sustained multi-dB shift) justifies it.

**Consolidated build-ready spec (all prior answers folded in):**

1. Exit hardening (cancel downloads, flush drafts/prefs, poison-safe abort) + scrollbar/fit retrofit + title-bar collapse support

4. Archive `<stem>.src.wav` beside `.md` + 3-state retention setting
5. Adaptive denoise as above (archival untouched, STT copy only)
6. Depth toggle + documentary video path + opt-in visible websearch (from earlier plan)

**Last two questions before I consider the plan frozen:**

1. Re-adapt UX: silent (log only) or a brief status flash (`room change — re-learning…`)? I recommend the flash — 2 s, non-blocking.
2. Calibration hint: show the `learning room tone…` indicator, or keep the first minute visually identical to normal recording? I recommend showing it — sets expectations for why the gate is gentle early.

//! Ollama library scanner: link GGUF weight blobs in place.
//!
//! Ollama keeps models as content-addressed blobs
//! (`<store>/blobs/sha256-<hex>`) described by JSON manifests
//! (`<store>/manifests/<registry>/<namespace>/<model>/<tag>`).
//! We only ever READ: resolve a model's weight blob and record its absolute
//! path. No copies, no downloads, no writes into the Ollama store.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// Weight layer media type in Ollama manifests.
const MODEL_LAYER: &str = "application/vnd.ollama.image.model";

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct OllamaModel {
    /// Display name: `model:tag`, or `namespace/model:tag` outside library.
    pub name: String,
    /// Absolute blob path (the file llama.cpp will load).
    pub blob: PathBuf,
    /// Expected byte size from the manifest (0 if unstated).
    pub bytes: u64,
    /// Blob digest hex (no `sha256:` prefix).
    pub digest: String,
}

/// Ollama models root: `$OLLAMA_MODELS`, else `%USERPROFILE%/.ollama/models`.
pub fn store_root() -> PathBuf {
    if let Some(v) = std::env::var_os("OLLAMA_MODELS") {
        if !v.is_empty() {
            return PathBuf::from(v);
        }
    }
    let home = std::env::var_os("USERPROFILE")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    home.join(".ollama").join("models")
}

/// Display name from manifest path components.
pub fn display_name(namespace: &str, model: &str, tag: &str) -> String {
    if namespace == "library" || namespace.is_empty() {
        format!("{model}:{tag}")
    } else {
        format!("{namespace}/{model}:{tag}")
    }
}

/// Parse one manifest document: `(weight digest hex, byte size)` of the first
/// `image.model` layer. Pure — unit-tested with fixture JSON.
pub fn parse_manifest(text: &str) -> Option<(String, u64)> {
    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text).ok()?;
    let layers = v.get("layers")?.as_array()?;
    for layer in layers {
        if layer.get("mediaType")?.as_str()? != MODEL_LAYER {
            continue;
        }
        let digest = layer.get("digest")?.as_str()?;
        let hex = digest.strip_prefix("sha256:")?.to_string();
        let size = layer.get("size")?.as_u64().unwrap_or(0);
        if hex.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) && !hex.is_empty() {
            return Some((hex, size));
        }
    }
    None
}

/// True when the file starts with the GGUF magic (`GGUF`). Reads 4 bytes.
pub fn gguf_magic_ok(path: &Path) -> bool {
    use std::io::Read;
    match std::fs::File::open(path) {
        Ok(mut f) => {
            let mut magic = [0u8; 4];
            matches!(f.read_exact(&mut magic), Ok(())) && &magic == b"GGUF"
        }
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {

## Yes — this is the complicated one. Revised plan deltas + deep questions (read-only)

You're right to feel the complexity: this turns the pipeline from "transcribe audio → summarize text" into "watch a film like a human, read about it, then explain it." Here's how your new specs land against the codebase, and where I need you to steer.

### What I heard (confirmed deltas)

- **Research: dynamic, up to 10 sources.** Not a fixed 5 — the count scales with the job (short/general = fewer, Deep documentary = up to 10), ranked by relevance, deduped. Summaries get **confirmed** before merging (my read: each source summary is checked against the film transcript/frames for contradictions, conflicts kept labeled, hallucinations dropped — confirm below).
- **Video goes last.** Order: STT → MAP notes → research (if ON) → **vision pass last** → joint REDUCE. Vision sees everything before it writes.
- **Third section: video transcription via Ollama.** This is the fork I need you on (see Q1) — today `ollama.rs` only **links GGUF weight blobs in place** (reads `%USERPROFILE%/.ollama/models`, never runs the Ollama server, never copies). "Transcription from Ollama" could mean two different architectures.
- **Adaptive film cutting.** 3-min vs 3-hour handled by extremity: dense sampling (~every 24 frames ≈ 1 fps @24fps → every cut, thematic beat, camera change caught) for Deep/short, sparse (~every 100 frames ≈ every ~4 s → general understanding) for light/long. Timestamps written to a temp doc; **video transcripts timestamped too** (new — audio path currently strips timestamps, `stt_whisper.cpp:33, validate.cpp:82` both set `print_timestamps=false`, `docs.rs:43` strips them).

- **Q5: recommended** — non-blocking toasts for learning/re-learn. Locked.

### How this maps to implementation (deltas from prior plan)

- STT gains a **timestamped mode for video only** (`[MM:SS] line` segments via `whisper_full_get_segment_t0/t1`; audio lectures keep today's clean untimed text). Both feed MAP, but video notes carry times through to REDUCE.
- Frame pipeline: `ffmpeg select='gt(scene,0.3)'` scene-cut detection **primary**, fixed-stride (24/100) as **fallback/cap** — pure stride on a 3 h film at 1 fps ≈ ~10 k frames, which no local VLM can swallow; scene cuts give you "every camera change" semantically instead of arithmetically. Frames → `<data>/frames/<job>/` (cache, swept by Clean caches), each captioned in 8–16-frame batches with `t=MM:SS`, captions appended to the temp doc you specified, then joint REDUCE writes the human-like themes cierre.
- Research module: relevance-ranked dynamic set (1–10), per-source summary + film-grounding check, conflicts labeled, cites as `source — claim`.
- Output `.md` for video: `## Summary / ## Visual analysis / ## Transcript (timestamped) / ## External context (web, if ON) / ## Audio` — video path never emits `.src.wav`, never writes into the source folder.

// Spilled variant: identical windowing, but PCM streams window-by-window
// from a raw float32LE sidecar instead of one giant RAM array. Used past
// SPILL_FLOATS (see pipeline.cpp) so 2-3h movies peak at one window plus
// the model instead of ~2GB. Model lifecycle matches stt_transcribe.
bool stt_transcribe_spilled(const std::string& pcm_path, size_t total_floats,
                            const SttConfig& cfg, std::string& out_text, std::string& err) {
    try {
        std::ifstream f(pcm_path, std::ios::binary);
        if (!f) {
            err = "cannot read spilled PCM";
            return false;
        }
        whisper_context* ctx = stt_open(cfg, err);
        if (!ctx) return false;
        const int win = (cfg.window_sec > 0 ? cfg.window_sec : 30) * 16000;
        const std::string lang = cfg.language.empty() ? "auto" : cfg.language;
        const bool tdrz = cfg.model_path.find("tdrz") != std::string::npos;
        int speaker = 1;
        bool need_label = tdrz;
        std::string out;
        std::vector<float> buf((size_t)win);
        bool ok = true;

        for (size_t off = 0; off < total_floats || total_floats == 0; off += (size_t)win) {
            size_t n = total_floats > off ? total_floats - off : 0;
            if (n > (size_t)win) n = (size_t)win;
            if (total_floats == 0) break;

            pv::progress_hook(PV_TRANSCRIBE, (float)off / (float)total_floats,
                              "Transcribing (spilled)...");
            if (!pv::checkpoint()) {
                err = "aborted";
                ok = false;
                break;
            }
            f.clear();
            f.seekg((std::streamoff)(off * sizeof(float)), std::ios::beg);
            f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(buf.data()), (std::streamsize)(n * sizeof(float)));
            if ((size_t)f.gcount() != n * sizeof(float)) {
                err = "spilled PCM truncated";
                ok = false;
                break;
            }
            if (!run_window(ctx, lang, tdrz, buf.data(), (int)n, out, speaker, need_label,
                            err)) {
                ok = false;
                break;
            }
            if (off + n >= total_floats) break;
        }
        whisper_free(ctx);
        if (!ok) return false;
        out_text = out;
        if (out_text.empty()) {
            err = "whisper produced no text";
            return false;
        }

## Responses to your 8 (plan mode — read-only, nothing changed)

**1. Ollama pattern — locked.** Keep in-place GGUF blob linking (`ollama.rs` scan → `gguf_magic_ok` → `record_link`, file never copied/moved). The video "third section" therefore runs on your already-downloaded Ollama weights loaded through our own llama.cpp VLM path — no server process, no drift. A linked Ollama VLM just appears as another `vision_models[]` entry per tier.

**2. Cross-instance matching + timestamps — yes, with one structural tweak.**
- *Your proposal works:* whisper emits **word-level timestamps internally**, then an LLM pass groups them into sentences and strips word times (`[00:01:03 word …]` → `[00:01:03–00:01:09] Sentence.`). Technically feasible — whisper.cpp exposes per-token timing (`whisper_full_get_token_data` / segment `t0/t1`; today both call sites set `print_timestamps=false` and read text-only, so this is additive, not a rewrite). Cost note: word timestamps inflate the STT-side token stream, but they're **discarded after grouping** — only sentence stamps persist, so MAP/REDUCE context doesn't bloat.
- *Cross-instance matching:* LLM-judge pass over **summaries** (never raw transcripts — cost), especially video-vs-documents. Your two-input design is right: (a) user declares "these go together" → check runs regardless; (b) AI auto-match runs at a **much looser threshold** than the merge suggester (`merge.rs` similarity) and only *proposes* ("these look related — compare?"), never merges silently. Unverified/cross-conflicting claims land in `## Unverified / conflicts, labeled`, per existing guide rules.
- *Timestamp↔video confirmation:* sentence times align against captioned frame times (`t=MM:SS`); a frame cited for a claim must fall inside (or adjacent to) the sentence window or it's flagged unverified. This is the "confirm timestamp with video" you asked for — cheap interval check, no new model.
- Follow-ups: sentence windows OK (not word-level persisted)? Should user-declared similarity live as a stored pair (persisted like `dismissed_groups`) or per-run only?

**3. Static depth-driven sampling (incl. the 10-hour case) — feasible on consumer hardware only with caps, and your "pieces then cleanup pass" is exactly the right shape.** Blunt math: 10 h × 1 fps (your 1/24 @24fps) ≈ **36,000 frames** — no consumer GPU captions all of those (at ~2–4 s/frame that's 20–40 hours). So the real design is: **scene-cut detection primary** (`ffmpeg select='gt(scene,…)'` catches every actual cut cheaply on CPU), stride (1/24 dense / mid / 1/100 sparse) as *fill between cuts*, **hard ceiling per film** (e.g. ~512 captioned frames; overflow handled by widening stride, logged as `kept N/M, stride S, cuts C`), caption shards MAP-reduced in 8–16-frame batches, then your cleanup pass fuses **frame → transcript → meaning** into the final text. A 10-hour Deep run still finishes — it just spends its frame budget on cuts + dense fill near dialogue-dense regions rather than literally every 24th frame. The "extensively long analysis in pieces, then passover" is the existing `reduce_long` hierarchical pattern reused for vision.
- Follow-ups: is a per-film frame budget ceiling acceptable (with the coverage line proving what was seen)? And should the cleanup pass be allowed to *drop* redundant frame captions (I recommend yes, logged)?

**4. Attention slider — I understand it now, and I recommend building it as exactly that.** Replace/augment the 3 depth presets with a 0–100 **Attention slider**: left = "smart person half-watching → overview" (sparse frames, short captions, short summary), right = "analyst annotating every shot → academic paper" (dense frames, technique captions, long hierarchical REDUCE + insight pass). Mid = today's Analytical. The slider drives sampling density, caption prompt detail, and REDUCE length target together. Calibration question below.

**5. Recommended — locked** (non-blocking toasts for learning/re-learn, nothing modal).

**6. Output shape — "watch then YouTube-summary with opinions" — confirmed with one guardrail.** Structure: `## What happens` (timestamped occurrences) → `## What it's about` (themes synthesis) → `## What the AI makes of it` (opinion, clearly fenced) → `## Summary` (the compressed whole) → transcript/research sections. The opinion section is first-class but **never mixes with facts** — that's what keeps a "what I thought" section trustworthy. Clarity ask: academic tone in the deep end and casual in the overview end (slider-driven register), or one consistent voice throughout?

**7. Video-only trigger (theme → compare against summarized + folder outputs) — realistic, with a scope guard.** Flow: video REDUCE emits a theme line → judge pass compares it against (a) other summaries in the current run and (b) existing `.md` summaries **in the same output folder** (summaries only, never raw; opt-out toggle; folder read is bounded, e.g. newest N). "Recommended" fallback holds: if the folder is huge/absent, degrade to in-run comparison only. Question: cap the folder scan (e.g. newest 20 summaries) — acceptable?

**8. Videos never touched + temp lifecycle — locked and thought through.** Video opened read-only in place (any path incl. UNC; conversions/frames live under `<data>/cache|frames|research/<job>/`, never beside the source). Temp shards (frame captions, timestamped transcript shards, per-batch notes) exist **only to bound context** — each is consumed by the next REDUCE stage, and on `PV_DONE` the job's temp dir is deleted; on abort/failure it's left for resume-then-swept by the existing Clean-caches orphan pass. Final artifacts are only the `.md` + sidecars (`.frames.md` kept cache-classed per your earlier call — confirm it also deletes on success, keeping just the coverage line?).

**2. "Frame budget ceiling + coverage line" — in short:** a 10-hour film at dense sampling produces more frames than any consumer GPU can caption (tens of thousands). The **coverage line** is one logged/proven line in the output (`Frames: captioned 512 of 2,140 sampled (stride 24, 311 scene cuts)`) so the analysis never pretends it saw more than it did. Nothing silent, nothing unbounded.

    /// Abort everything (backend abort + clear + epoch) and return all files
    /// to Input.
    pub fn abort_all(&mut self) -> usize {
        let n = self.processing.len();
        let _ = self.queue.abort_all();
        for p in self.processing.drain(..) {
            if let Some(inp) = self.input.iter_mut().find(|x| x.id == p.id) {
                inp.state = FileState::Queued;
            }
        }
        self.paused = false;
        self.status = "Aborted — files returned to Input.".to_string();
        self.check_drained();
        n
    }

    // ---------------- M4: models / downloads / wizard ----------------

    /// Re-read the inventory snapshot from disk + manifest.
    /// Links whose files vanished are removed first (user moved/deleted
    /// them) so stale paths can never linger.
    pub fn refresh_models(&mut self) {
        let dir = pv_backend::dirs::models_dir();
        let mut man = pv_backend::manifest::read(&dir);
        let dead = pv_backend::manifest::prune_missing_links(&mut man);
        if !dead.is_empty() {
            let _ = pv_backend::manifest::write(&dir, &man);
            self.status = format!("Removed {} missing link(s).", dead.len());
        }
        match pv_backend::models::status() {
            Ok(snap) => {
                self.models = snap.models;
                self.models_dir = snap.models_dir;
                self.active_stt = snap.active_stt;
                self.active_llm = snap.active_llm;
            }
            Err(e) => self.status = format!("Models unreadable: {e}"),
        }
    }

    /// Persist current session texts to the draft folder + index.
    pub fn persist_review(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        let r = self.review.clone().ok_or("no review open")?;
        let undo = r.undo.clone().map(|u| pv_backend::drafts::DraftUndo {
            left: u.left,
            right: u.right,
            center: u.center,
            merged: u.merged,
        });
        pv_backend::drafts::save_draft(&r.stem, &r.left, &r.right, &r.center, r.merged, r.dirty, undo)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn update_review_texts(&mut self, left: String, right: String, center: String) {
        if let Some(r) = self.review.as_mut() {
            if r.left != left || r.right != right || r.center != center {
                r.left = left;
                r.right = right;
                r.center = center;
                r.dirty = true;
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn mark_review_dirty(&mut self) {
        if let Some(r) = self.review.as_mut() {
            r.dirty = true;
        }
    }

    fn snap_review(&mut self) {
        if let Some(r) = self.review.as_mut() {
            r.undo = Some(RevSnapData {
                left: r.left.clone(),
                right: r.right.clone(),
                center: r.center.clone(),
                merged: r.merged,
            });
        }
    }

```
    /// Cancel all in-flight model downloads (best-effort, never blocks).
    /// Mid-`rename(part→dest)` exits otherwise leave truncated models behind.
    pub fn cancel_downloads(&self) {
        if let Some(dl) = &self.downloader {
            dl.cancel_all();
        }
    }

    /// Single quit-path entry: flush drafts + prefs, cancel downloads, then
    /// abort the backend. Every step is best-effort so shutdown can never
    /// hang — callers always `process::exit(0)` afterwards (which skips
    /// `CoreLib` Drop/`FreeLibrary` while a worker may still run in the DLL).
    /// Future shutdown work (recorder stop, VLM temp sweep) hooks in here.
    pub fn shutdown_prepare(&mut self) {
        // Review widgets flush into `self.review` on every keystroke, so the
        // session holds the latest text even though disk persistence is
        // debounced — persist it now so quit never loses the last edits.
        let _ = self.persist_review();
        self.save_prefs();
        self.cancel_downloads();
        let _ = self.abort_all();
    }
```

```
        shutdown_trace("quit hook fired");
        // Poison-safe: a poisoned store lock must still attempt the abort —
        // skipping it would reopen the FreeLibrary-while-worker-runs crash.
        let store_opt = QUIT_STORE
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .clone();
        if let Some(store) = store_opt {
            let _ = store.update(cx, |st, _| {
                st.shutdown_prepare();
            });
            shutdown_trace("drafts+prefs+downloads flushed");
        } else {
            shutdown_trace("no store published, skipping flush");
        }
```

```
    fn on_quit(&mut self, _: &Quit, _: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) {
        // Stop the worker at a safe point first; files stay queued.
        // Mirrors install_quit_hook: single shutdown_prepare covers drafts,
        // prefs, downloads, and the backend abort — always ends in exit(0)
        // to skip DLL teardown while a worker may run inside it.
        crate::shutdown_trace("alt-q quit action fired");
        self.store.update(cx, |st, _| {
            st.shutdown_prepare();
        });
        crate::shutdown_trace("alt-q backend aborted, exiting");
        std::process::exit(0);
    }
```

/// List mode: compact fixed-width rows that flow into multiple columns.
fn staged_list_row(
    f: &InputFile,
    warning: Option<String>,
    checked: bool,
    store: Entity<Store>,
    dark: bool,
) -> impl IntoElement {
    let path_str = f.path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
    h_flex()
        .gap_2()
        .p_1()
        .w(px(260.))
        .bg(rgb(theme::surface(dark)))
        .child(div().child(kind_glyph(f)).font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD))
        .child(
            div()
                .flex_1()
                .truncate()
                .child(short_name(f))
                .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD),
        )
        .child(merge_check(f.id, checked, store.clone()))
        .child(match warning {
            Some(reason) => warn_button(path_str, reason, store.clone()),
            None => div().into_any_element(),
        })
        .child(delete_button(f.id, store))
        .into_any_element()
}

/// Details mode: one full-width explorer-like row per file.
fn staged_details_row(
    f: &InputFile,
    warning: Option<String>,
    checked: bool,
    store: Entity<Store>,
    dark: bool,
) -> impl IntoElement {
    let path_str = f.path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
    h_flex()
        .gap_2()
        .p_1()
        .bg(rgb(theme::surface(dark)))
        .child(div().child(kind_glyph(f)).font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD))
        .child(
            div()
                .flex_1()
                .truncate()
                .child(path_str.clone())
                .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD),
        )
        .child(div().child(fmt_size(f.size)).font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD))
        .child(
            div()
                .child(format!("{:?}", f.state))
                .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD),
        )
        .child(merge_check(f.id, checked, store.clone()))
        .child(match warning {
            Some(reason) => warn_button(path_str, reason, store.clone()),
            None => div().into_any_element(),
        })
        .child(delete_button(f.id, store))
        .into_any_element()
}

fn staged_card(
    f: &InputFile,
    warning: Option<String>,
    checked: bool,
    mode: ViewMode,
    store: Entity<Store>,
    dark: bool,
) -> gpui_kit::AnyElement {
    match mode {
        ViewMode::Large => staged_tile(f, warning, checked, store, dark).into_any_element(),
        ViewMode::List => staged_list_row(f, warning, checked, store, dark).into_any_element(),
        ViewMode::Details => staged_details_row(f, warning, checked, store, dark).into_any_element(),
    }
}

fn scan_section(
    scan: &[pv_backend::ollama::OllamaModel],
    store: &Entity<Store>,
) -> impl IntoElement {
    if scan.is_empty() {
        return div().into_any_element();
    }
    let store_l = store.clone();
    let store_s = store.clone();
    let rows: Vec<_> = scan
        .iter()
        .map(|m| {
            let name = m.name.clone();
            let gb = m.bytes as f64 / 1073741824.0;
            let store_l = store_l.clone();
            let store_s = store_s.clone();
            let name_l = name.clone();
            let name_s = name.clone();
            h_flex()
                .gap_2()
                .flex_wrap()
                .child(
                    div()
                        .flex_1()
                        .truncate()
                        .child(format!("{} ({:.1} GB)", name, gb))
                        .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD),
                )
                .child(
                    Button::new(format!("set-llm-{name_l}"))
                        .label("Set as Summarizing (LLM)")
                        .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD)
                        .on_click(move |_, _, cx| {
                            let name = name_l.clone();
                            store_l.update(cx, |s, cx| {
                                if let Err(e) = s.link_ollama(&name, "llm") {
                                    s.status = format!("Link failed: {e}");
                                } else {
                                    let cur = s.active_stt.clone();
                                    let linked = format!("ollama:{name}");
                                    s.set_active_pair(&cur, &linked);
                                }
                                cx.notify();
                            });
                        }),
                )
                .child(
                    Button::new(format!("set-stt-{name_s}"))
                        .label("Set as Transcribing (STT)")
                        .font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD)
                        .on_click(move |_, _, cx| {
                            let name = name_s.clone();
                            store_s.update(cx, |s, cx| {
                                if let Err(e) = s.link_ollama(&name, "stt") {
                                    s.status = format!("Link failed: {e}");
                                } else {
                                    let cur = s.active_llm.clone();
                                    let linked = format!("ollama:{name}");
                                    s.set_active_pair(&linked, &cur);
                                }
                                cx.notify();
                            });
                        }),
                )
        })
        .collect();
    v_flex()
        .gap_1()
        .child(
            div()
                .child("Ollama library — link into a column:")
                .font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD),
        )
        .children(rows)
        .into_any_element()
}

                row = row.child(
                    Button::new(format!("set-llm-{id_l}"))

        // exactly one column. Catalog roles are fixed; linked models carry

        let llm_models: Vec<_> = models

# UI version pins (pinned + tracked, revisited quarterly)

| Crate | Pin | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `gpui-kit` (facade) | `=0.6.1` | Blessed boot (`application()` + `init()` + `Root`); mirrors kit hello_world |
| `gpui-component` | `=0.6.1` | Comes via the facade; never depended on directly |
| `gpui-pre` (package) | `=0.3.1` | Comes via the facade; never depended on directly |
| `embed-resource` (build-dep) | `=3.0.11` | Embeds `assets/voice.ico` into the exe; established, tiny |
| `rfd` | `0.15` | Native file dialogs; semver range is fine (leaf UI dep) |
| `async-channel` | `2` | Backend→UI event bridge; semver range is fine (leaf dep) |
| `zip` (backend) | `=2.4.2` | OOXML/ODF/EPUB containers for the offline document extractor |
| `quick-xml` (backend) | `=0.36.2` | Streaming `w:t`/`a:t`/`text:p` text nodes for the extractor |
| `calamine` (backend) | `=0.24.0` | `xlsx`/`xls`/`ods` sheets → markdown tables; pure Rust |
| `encoding_rs` (backend) | `=0.8.41` | UTF-16/Windows-1252 fallback decoding for plain-text docs |
| `pdf-extract` (backend) | `=0.7.12` | Text-layer PDF extraction; scanned PDFs warn instead of OCR |

## Facade doctrine (burned twice, recorded forever)

`app/` depends on **`gpui-kit` only** for UI. The kit re-exports the matched
set (`use gpui_kit::*` is GPUI itself), so versions cannot drift apart.
Direct `gpui` / `gpui-component` dependencies are banned — depending on both
the facade and the raw crates risks duplicate-type graphs.

## The critical decision

`gpui-component 0.6.1` does **not** depend on Zed's `gpui` crate at all. It builds on
`gpui-pre ^0.3.1` (+ `gpui-base`, `gpui-pre-macros`). Depending on both `gpui 0.2.2`
and `gpui-component 0.6.1` would compile **two different UI frameworks** into one
binary with mutually incompatible types. So: `gpui-pre` only, never `gpui`.

Naming trap (burned us once): the package is `gpui-pre` but its **lib target is
named `gpui`** — exactly like `gpui-component` itself declares it
(`gpui = { version, package = "gpui-pre" }`). Our `app/Cargo.toml` does the
same rename, so code reads `use gpui::...`. If `use gpui_pre::` ever reappears,
the build fails with E0432/E0433 — that is the tripwire working.

## Track policy (pin and track)

- `=` pins in `app/Cargo.toml` + committed `Cargo.lock`. Never float.
- Quarterly: `cargo update -p gpui-pre -p gpui-component`, then full rebuild +
  `node tests/smoke.mjs` + build-machine proof before committing the new lock.
- Never upgrade mid-milestone.

## Known upstream issues

- `gpui-pre-macros 0.3.1` fails **release** builds with E0433
  (`derive_inspector_reflection` referenced but cfg'd out when
  `debug_assertions` are off). Worked around via
  `[profile.release] debug-assertions = true` in the workspace root.
  Re-evaluate each quarterly review; drop the override once a fixed
  `gpui-pre` is pinned.

## M0 proof (run on a networked Windows machine)

```powershell
cargo tree -i gpui-pre          # exactly ONE gpui-pre version; no `gpui` (Zed) in graph
cargo build --workspace         # app window opens, shows M0 placeholder
cargo test -p pv-backend        # dirs + health unit tests
```

## Build-time note

First-time compilation of the GPU stack (`gpui-pre` + `gpui-component`:
Blade graphics, cosmic-text, font-kit) is slow — tens of minutes in release,
faster in dev profile. This is inherent, not a hang: `gpui-component` ships
with an empty default feature set (no tree-sitter weight), so there is nothing
to trim. Watch Task Manager: `rustc` pinned + RAM headroom = just wait. Use
`build.ps1 -Dev` for iteration; reserve `--release` for shipping.

//! pv-backend: framework-free backend for Present Voice.
//!
//! Port of the ex-Tauri `main.rs` shell minus all Tauri coupling. The GPUI app
//! in `app/` drives this crate through plain Rust calls; progress flows back
//! over [`Event`] channels the UI forwards into its executor.
//!
//! Audit-bug ledger (each fixed here, not in UI code):
//! - stable file identity (path-keyed, never FIFO index),
//! - abort epochs (stale pre-abort DONE events are dropped),
//! - option lifecycle (no resurrection of removed files),
//! - single-lock shared state (no ABBA deadlock),
//! - output confinement (no traversal, extension whitelist),
//! - poison-safe locks (no `unwrap` on any `Mutex`).

pub mod catalog;
pub mod core_bridge;
pub mod diag;
pub mod dirs;
pub mod docs;
pub mod download;
pub mod drafts;
pub mod manifest;
pub mod merge;
pub mod models;
pub mod ollama;
pub mod prefs;
pub mod progress;
pub mod queue;

pub use progress::Event;

/// M0 liveness probe (replaced by real health in M1 widening).
pub fn health() -> &'static str {
    "pv-backend ok"
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::health;

    #[test]
    fn health_reports_ok() {
        assert_eq!(health(), "pv-backend ok");
    }
}

```
/// Display name for a device (best-effort; never fails).
fn dev_name(d: &cpal::Device) -> String {
    d.description()
        .map(|desc| desc.name().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "(unnamed device)".to_string())
}

/// Input device names (best-effort: empty when the audio subsystem is down).
pub fn list_devices() -> Vec<String> {
    let host = cpal::default_host();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(devs) = host.input_devices() {
        for d in devs {
            out.push(dev_name(&d));
        }
    }
    out.sort();
```

```
    /// Stop capture and finalize the WAV header. The file stays on disk —
    /// caller decides send-to-queue vs discard.
    pub fn stop(self) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
        self.shared.stop.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        // Dropping the stream first ends the callback; then finalize.
        let path = self.path.clone();
        let shared = self.shared.clone();
        drop(self._stream);
        shared
            .writer
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "recorder lock poisoned".to_string())?
            .finalize()?;
        Ok(path)
    }
}

/// Take length in whole seconds from the file header (cheap open, no decode).
pub fn take_secs(path: &PathBuf) -> u64 {
    let Ok(r) = hound::WavReader::open(path) else {
        return 0;
    };
    let spec = r.spec();
    if spec.sample_rate == 0 || spec.channels == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    r.len() as u64 / spec.channels as u64 / spec.sample_rate as u64
}

struct PlayShared {
    reader: Mutex<hound::WavReader<std::io::BufReader<std::fs::File>>>,
    file_rate: u32,
    file_ch: u16,
    out_rate: u32,
    out_ch: u16,
    /// Fractional file-frame position (linear resample cursor).
    pos: Mutex<f64>,
    total_frames: u64,
    stop: AtomicBool,
    done: AtomicBool,
}

/// Playback handle for a finished take. Dropping stops the sound; the file
/// is untouched. Pause = drop + remember `pos_frames()`; resume = `play`
/// again from that offset.
pub struct Player {
    _stream: cpal::Stream,
    shared: Arc<PlayShared>,
    pub path: PathBuf,
}

impl Player {
    pub fn play(path: &PathBuf, offset_frames: u64) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let spec = reader.spec();
        if spec.sample_rate == 0 || spec.channels == 0 {
            return Err("unreadable take".to_string());
        }
        let total_frames = reader.len() as u64 / spec.channels.max(1) as u64;
        let host = cpal::default_host();
        let dev = host
            .default_output_device()
            .ok_or_else(|| "no output device found".to_string())?;
        let cfg = dev
            .default_output_config()
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot open output ({e})"))?;
        let out_rate = cfg.sample_rate();
        let out_ch = cfg.channels();
        let shared = Arc::new(PlayShared {
            reader: Mutex::new(reader),
            file_rate: spec.sample_rate,
            file_ch: spec.channels,
            out_rate,
            out_ch,
            pos: Mutex::new(offset_frames as f64),
            total_frames,
            stop: AtomicBool::new(false),
            done: AtomicBool::new(false),
        });
        let worker = Arc::clone(&shared);
        // Prime past the resume offset (hound has no seek-to-frame here).
        if offset_frames > 0 {
            if let Ok(mut r) = worker.reader.lock() {
                let mut skip = offset_frames * spec.channels.max(1) as u64;
                let mut buf = [0i32; 512];
                while skip > 0 {
                    let n = skip.min(512) as usize;
                    let mut got = 0;
                    for s in r.samples::<i32>().take(n) {
                        if s.is_ok() {
                            got += 1;
                        } else {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    let _ = buf;
                    if got == 0 {
                        break;
                    }
                    skip -= got as u64;
                }
            }
            if let Ok(mut p) = worker.pos.lock() {
                *p = offset_frames as f64;
            }
        }
        let stream = dev
            .build_output_stream(
                cfg.config(),
                move |data: &mut [f32], _| {
                    if worker.stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                        data.fill(0.0);
                        return;
                    }
                    let Ok(mut r) = worker.reader.lock() else {
                        data.fill(0.0);
                        return;
                    };
                    let Ok(mut pos) = worker.pos.lock() else {
                        data.fill(0.0);
                        return;
                    };
                    let step = worker.file_rate as f64 / worker.out_rate.max(1) as f64;
                    let fch = worker.file_ch.max(1) as usize;
                    let och = worker.out_ch.max(1) as usize;
                    let mut frames = r.samples::<i32>();
                    // One-sample lookahead is skipped for simplicity: nearest
                    // file frame per output frame (voice-memo grade).
                    let mut di = 0;
                    while di < data.len() {
                        if *pos >= worker.total_frames as f64 {
                            worker.done.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
                            data[di..].fill(0.0);
                            break;
                        }
                        let want = pos.floor() as u64;
                        // Advance the reader to `want` (monotone cursor).
                        // Reader position tracks `consumed`; skip the gap.
                        let consumed = (*pos - (*pos % 1.0)) as u64;
                        let _ = (want, consumed);
                        // Pull one file frame (nearest): read next frame and
                        // use it directly — the cursor only ever advances, so
                        // sequential reads stay in lockstep with `pos`.
                        let mut frame = vec![0.0f32; fch];
                        let mut ok = true;
                        for c in 0..fch {
                            match frames.next() {
                                Some(Ok(s)) => frame[c] = s as f32 / 8_388_608.0,
                                _ => {
                                    ok = false;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        if !ok {
                            worker.done.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
                            data[di..].fill(0.0);
                            break;
                        }
                        *pos += step;
                        // Map channels: mono→dup, multi→first/min mix.
                        for o in 0..och {
                            if di >= data.len() {
                                break;
                            }
                            data[di] = if fch == 1 {
                                frame[0]
                            } else if o < fch {
                                frame[o]
                            } else {
                                frame[0]
                            };
                            di += 1;
                        }
                    }
                },
                |_| {},
                None,
            )
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot play ({e})"))?;
        stream.play().map_err(|e| format!("cannot play ({e})"))?;
        Ok(Player {
            _stream: stream,
            shared,
            path: path.clone(),
        })
    }

    pub fn is_done(&self) -> bool {
        self.shared.done.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    pub fn pos_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.shared
            .pos
            .lock()
            .map(|p| p.floor() as u64)
            .unwrap_or(0)
    }

    pub fn stop(self) {
        self.shared.stop.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }
}
```

```
    /// Single quit-path entry: flush drafts + prefs, cancel downloads, then
    /// abort the backend. Every step is best-effort so shutdown can never
    /// hang — callers always `process::exit(0)` afterwards (which skips
    /// `CoreLib` Drop/`FreeLibrary` while a worker may still run in the DLL).
    /// Future shutdown work (recorder stop, VLM temp sweep) hooks in here.
    pub fn shutdown_prepare(&mut self) {
        // Stop any live capture first: the take file is kept on disk (never
        // auto-deleted) so nothing recorded is lost to the exit.
        self.rec_shutdown();
        // Review widgets flush into `self.review` on every keystroke, so the
        // session holds the latest text even though disk persistence is
        // debounced — persist it now so quit never loses the last edits.
        let _ = self.persist_review();
        self.save_prefs();
        self.cancel_downloads();
        let _ = self.abort_all();
    }

    /// Navigate between pages. Leaving Record with an unsent finished take
    /// auto-stages it to Input (per spec) — recording in progress is never
    /// touched, and already-sent takes are not duplicated.
    pub fn goto_page(&mut self, page: Page) {
        if self.page == Page::Record && page != Page::Record {
            self.rec_auto_stage();
        }
        self.page = page;
    }

    // ---------------- Record page: transport + takes ----------------

    /// Capture devices for the Record picker (empty when audio is down).
    pub fn rec_devices(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        pv_backend::record::list_devices()
    }

    /// Rates the chosen device reports (empty = query failed → native only).
    pub fn rec_device_rates(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
        match &self.rec_device {
            Some(n) => pv_backend::record::device_rates(n),
            None => Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn rec_status_line(&self) -> String {
        let len = pv_backend::record::fmt_len(self.rec_samples, self.rec_rate);
        let fmt = if self.rec_rate > 0 {
            format!("{} Hz", self.rec_rate)
        } else {
            "—".to_string()
        };
        let ch = match self.rec_channels {
            1 => "mono".to_string(),
            n if n > 1 => format!("{n}ch"),
            _ => "—".to_string(),
        };
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Empty => "Empty — press Record.".to_string(),
            RecStatus::Recording => {
                format!("● REC {len} · 24-bit/{fmt} {ch} · peak {} · clips {} · learning room tone…",
                    self.rec_peak_db, self.rec_clips)
            }
            RecStatus::Paused => format!("❚❚ PAUSED {len} · press Record to resume."),
            RecStatus::Stopped => {
                let total = pv_backend::record::fmt_secs(self.rec_total_secs);
                let tail = if self.rec_sent { " · sent to Input ✓" } else { " · unsent take" };
                format!("■ STOPPED {total}{tail}")
            }
            RecStatus::Playing => {
                let total = pv_backend::record::fmt_secs(self.rec_total_secs);
                let pos = pv_backend::record::fmt_len(self.rec_play_pos, self.rec_rate);
                format!("▶ PLAYING {pos}/{total}")
            }
            RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                let total = pv_backend::record::fmt_secs(self.rec_total_secs);
                let pos = pv_backend::record::fmt_len(self.rec_play_pos, self.rec_rate);
                format!("❚❚ PLAY PAUSED {pos}/{total}")
            }
        }
    }

    /// Start (or resume) capture. Resuming after pause continues the SAME
    /// take file by appending a fresh recorder onto it — no: pause keeps the
    /// stream open and drops samples, so resume is seamless on one file.
    pub fn rec_start(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Paused => {
                if let Some(r) = &self.recorder {
                    r.set_paused(false);
                    self.rec_status = RecStatus::Recording;
                    self.status = "Recording resumed.".to_string();
                    return Ok(());
                }
                // Stream died while paused: fall through to a fresh take.
            }
            RecStatus::Recording => return Ok(()),
            RecStatus::Playing | RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                self.rec_play_stop_silent();
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        // Fresh take (previous finished take must be sent/cleared first).
        if self.rec_status == RecStatus::Stopped && !self.rec_sent {
            return Err("Send or Clear the finished take first.".to_string());
        }
        let rec = pv_backend::record::Recorder::start(
            self.rec_device.as_deref(),
            self.rec_rate_opt,
        )?;
        self.rec_rate = rec.sample_rate;
        self.rec_channels = rec.channels;
        self.rec_samples = 0;
        self.rec_peaks.clear();
        self.rec_peak_db = "-inf dB".to_string();
        self.rec_clips = 0;
        self.rec_play_pos = 0;
        self.rec_total_secs = 0;
        self.rec_sent = false;
        self.rec_path = None;
        self.recorder = Some(rec);
        self.rec_status = RecStatus::Recording;
        self.status = "Recording…".to_string();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Pause capture (take file stays open; timer frozen — sample-counted).
    /// Pause during playback pauses playback instead (position kept).
    pub fn rec_pause(&mut self) {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Recording => {
                if let Some(r) = &self.recorder {
                    r.set_paused(true);
                }
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::Paused;
                self.status = "Recording paused.".to_string();
            }
            RecStatus::Playing => {
                if let Some(p) = self.player.take() {
                    self.rec_play_pos = p.pos_frames();
                    p.stop();
                }
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::PlayPaused;
                self.status = "Playback paused.".to_string();
            }
            RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                // Resume playback from the held position.
                self.rec_play_from(self.rec_play_pos);
            }
            RecStatus::Paused => {
                // Resume capture (same as Record while paused).
                let _ = self.rec_start();
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Stop capture, finalize the WAV header, keep the file. Never deletes.
    pub fn rec_stop(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Recording | RecStatus::Paused => {
                let rec = self.recorder.take().ok_or("nothing recording")?;
                let rate = rec.sample_rate;
                let path = rec.stop()?;
                self.rec_total_secs = pv_backend::record::take_secs(&path);
                self.rec_rate = rate;
                self.rec_samples = self.rec_total_secs * rate as u64;
                self.rec_path = Some(path);
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::Stopped;
                self.rec_sent = false;
                self.status = "Take kept — Send to Input or Clear.".to_string();
                Ok(())
            }
            RecStatus::Playing | RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                self.rec_play_stop_silent();
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::Stopped;
                self.status = "Playback stopped.".to_string();
                Ok(())
            }
            _ => Err("Nothing to stop.".to_string()),
        }
    }

    /// Play the finished take (or resume from pause position).
    pub fn rec_play(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Stopped => self.rec_play_from(0),
            RecStatus::PlayPaused => self.rec_play_from(self.rec_play_pos),
            RecStatus::Playing => Ok(()),
            _ => Err("Stop recording first, then play the take.".to_string()),
        }
    }

    fn rec_play_from(&mut self, offset: u64) {
        let path = match &self.rec_path {
            Some(p) => p.clone(),
            None => {
                self.status = "No take to play.".to_string();
                return;
            }
        };
        match pv_backend::record::Player::play(&path, offset) {
            Ok(p) => {
                self.player = Some(p);
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::Playing;
                self.status = "Playing take…".to_string();
            }
            Err(e) => {
                self.status = format!("Playback failed: {e}");
            }
        }
    }

    fn rec_play_stop_silent(&mut self) {
        if let Some(p) = self.player.take() {
            self.rec_play_pos = p.pos_frames();
            p.stop();
        }
    }

    /// Poll live counters (called from the Record view's refresh tick).
    /// Detects natural playback end and returns to Stopped.
    pub fn rec_poll(&mut self) {
        if let Some(r) = &self.recorder {
            if matches!(self.rec_status, RecStatus::Recording | RecStatus::Paused) {
                self.rec_samples = r.samples();
                self.rec_peaks = r.peaks();
                self.rec_peak_db = r.peak_db();
                self.rec_clips = r.clips();
            }
        }
        if let Some(p) = &self.player {
            if self.rec_status == RecStatus::Playing {
                self.rec_play_pos = p.pos_frames();
                if p.is_done() {
                    self.player.take().map(|p| p.stop());
                    self.rec_status = RecStatus::Stopped;
                    self.status = "Playback finished.".to_string();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Discard the finished take file (explicit Clear only — never automatic).
    pub fn rec_clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Recording | RecStatus::Paused | RecStatus::Playing | RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                return Err("Stop first, then Clear.".to_string());
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        if let Some(p) = self.rec_path.take() {
            std::fs::remove_file(&p).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
        self.rec_status = RecStatus::Empty;
        self.rec_samples = 0;
        self.rec_peaks.clear();
        self.rec_total_secs = 0;
        self.rec_play_pos = 0;
        self.rec_sent = false;
        self.status = "Take cleared.".to_string();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Stage the finished take into Input for transcription. Videos are
    /// never touched by this path — only Record takes and picked files.
    pub fn rec_send_to_input(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        let path = self.rec_path.clone().ok_or("No take to send.")?;
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Stopped | RecStatus::PlayPaused => {}
            _ => return Err("Stop the take first.".to_string()),
        }
        self.rec_play_stop_silent();
        self.add_files(vec![path]);
        self.rec_sent = true;
        self.status = "Take sent to Input ✓".to_string();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Auto-stage on navigating away with an unsent finished take.
    /// Best-effort: failures only set the status line, never block nav.
    fn rec_auto_stage(&mut self) {
        if self.rec_status == RecStatus::Stopped && !self.rec_sent && self.rec_path.is_some() {
            let _ = self.rec_send_to_input();
        }
    }

    /// Quit-path: finalize any live capture, keeping the file. Never deletes.
    fn rec_shutdown(&mut self) {
        if matches!(self.rec_status, RecStatus::Recording | RecStatus::Paused) {
            let _ = self.rec_stop();
        }
        if self.player.is_some() {
            self.rec_play_stop_silent();
            if self.rec_status == RecStatus::Playing || self.rec_status == RecStatus::PlayPaused {
                self.rec_status = RecStatus::Stopped;
            }
        }
    }
```

/// blocking receive, async channel hop, UI task for application.
/// Shared by pipeline runs and model downloads.
pub fn spawn_pump(store: Entity<Store>, rx: Receiver<Event>, cx: &mut App) {
    let (atx, arx) = async_channel::bounded(256);
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        for ev in rx {
            if atx.send_blocking(ev).is_err() {
                break;
            }
        }
    });
    let pump = store;
    cx.spawn(async move |cx| {
        while let Ok(ev) = arx.recv().await {
            let pump = pump.clone();
            cx.update(|cx| {
                pump.update(cx, |s, cx| {
                    s.apply_event(ev);
                    cx.notify();
                })
            });
        }
    })
    .detach();
}

    fn esc(s: &str) -> String {
        let mut o = String::with_capacity(s.len());
        for c in s.chars() {
            match c {
                '"' => o.push_str("\\\""),
                '\\' => o.push_str("\\\\"),
                '\n' => o.push_str("\\n"),
                '\r' => o.push_str("\\r"),
                '\t' => o.push_str("\\t"),
                c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => o.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
                c => o.push(c),
            }

```
    /// Play the finished take (or resume from pause position).
    pub fn rec_play(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        match self.rec_status {
            RecStatus::Stopped => {
                self.rec_play_from(0);
                Ok(())
            }
            RecStatus::PlayPaused => {
                let pos = self.rec_play_pos;
                self.rec_play_from(pos);
                Ok(())
            }
            RecStatus::Playing => Ok(()),
            _ => Err("Stop recording first, then play the take.".to_string()),
        }
    }
```

```
    #[test]
    fn shutdown_prepare_flushes_and_aborts_without_hanging() {
        // Best-effort quit path: no review open, no downloader, sim backend.
        // Must drain processing and never panic — exit(0) follows in prod.
        let mut s = staged_proc();
        s.paused = true;
        s.shutdown_prepare();
        assert!(s.processing.is_empty());
        assert!(!s.paused);
        assert!(s.input.iter().all(|f| f.state == FileState::Queued));
        // Idempotent: second call (alt-q + app-quit double-fire) is safe.
        s.shutdown_prepare();
        assert!(s.processing.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rec_transport_guards_empty_state() {
        let mut s = Store::new();
        assert_eq!(s.rec_status, RecStatus::Empty);
        assert!(s.rec_stop().is_err());
        assert!(s.rec_clear().is_ok()); // clearing nothing is a no-op success
        assert!(s.rec_send_to_input().is_err());
        assert!(s.rec_play().is_err());
        assert!(s.rec_status_line().contains("Empty"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rec_auto_stage_moves_unsent_take_on_nav() {
        let mut s = Store::new();
        // Fake a finished take (no hardware needed — path only).
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("pv-rec-nav-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);
        let wav = dir.join("take.wav");
        std::fs::write(&wav, b"RIFFfake").unwrap();
        s.rec_status = RecStatus::Stopped;
        s.rec_path = Some(wav.clone());
        s.rec_sent = false;
        s.page = Page::Record;
        // WAV content is not validated here (STT validates at Start).
        s.goto_page(Page::Input);
        assert_eq!(s.page, Page::Input);
        assert!(s.rec_sent);
        assert!(s.input.iter().any(|f| f.path == wav));
        // Staying put never duplicates.
        let n = s.input.len();
        s.goto_page(Page::Input);
        assert_eq!(s.input.len(), n);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
```

    /// Add staged files (deduped by path). Single + batch arrive together.
    /// Audio → STT path; modern documents → extraction path. Anything else
    /// is skipped with a `file_warnings` entry + Error Center record.
    /// Single source of truth for the gate (pickers use it too).
    pub fn add_files(&mut self, paths: Vec<PathBuf>) {
        for path in paths {
            if self.input.iter().any(|f| f.path == path) {
                continue;
            }
            let ext = path
                .extension()
                .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
                .map(|e| e.to_lowercase())
                .unwrap_or_default();
            if BAD_EXTS.contains(&ext.as_str()) {
                let reason = format!(
                    "Export as .wav/.mp3/.flac/.opus first — .{} is an Audacity project format, not raw audio.",
                    ext
                );
                self.file_warnings.insert(path.clone(), reason.clone());

    /// Open (or seed) the persistent draft for an output.
    pub fn open_review(&mut self, id: u64) -> Result<(), String> {
        // Heal first so a dead session can never linger underneath the new one.
        self.heal_review();
        let o = self.output.iter().find(|o| o.id == id).cloned().ok_or("output not found")?;
        let d = pv_backend::drafts::open_draft(id, &o.md_name, &o.raw, &o.summary)?;

            md_name: o.md_name,

            right: d.right,
            center: d.center,
            merged: d.meta.merged,
            dirty: d.meta.dirty,
            undo: d.meta.undo.map(|u| RevSnapData {
                left: u.left,
                right: u.right,
                center: u.center,
                merged: u.merged,
            }),
        });
        self.refresh_draft_badges();
        Ok(())
    }

/// Extract an integer from a tiny sidecar JSON blob (`"key":12345`) without
/// pulling serde into `app`. Returns None when absent/unparseable.
fn sidecar_int(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<i64> {
    let pat = format!("\"{key}\":");
    let i = text.find(&pat)? + pat.len();
    let rest = text[i..].trim_start().as_bytes();
    let mut j = 0;
    if j < rest.len() && rest[j] == b'-' {
        j += 1;
    }
    let start = j;
    while j < rest.len() && rest[j].is_ascii_digit() {
        j += 1;
    }
    if j == start {
        return None;
    }
    text[i..i + j].parse().ok()
}

```
/// Source retention after success: "keep" | "delete" | "archive".
/// Anything else (including legacy missing keys) keeps originals.
fn normalize_retention(m: &str) -> String {
    match m {
        "delete" | "archive" => m.to_string(),
        _ => "keep".to_string(),
    }
}

/// Pre-STT denoise: "recommended" | "off" | "aggressive".
fn normalize_denoise(m: &str) -> String {
    match m {
        "off" | "aggressive" => m.to_string(),
        _ => "recommended".to_string(),
    }
}
```
